text:
olga: Quick question — setting up client to hit a private VPC endpoint behind an outbound HTTP proxy. Using CUSTOM_BASE_URL env and also setting HTTP(S)_PROXY. I'm seeing 502s on streaming requests only. Anyone seen ordering/precedence issues with base_url vs proxy? Example:
```
export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://private-inference.internal
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128
node ./example-stream.js
```
Streaming errors look like `ERR_HTTP2_CONNECTION` or chunks stop after a few tokens.

devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/vpc-proxy-config — see "proxy host header override" and the note about proxies that don't support HTTP/2.

marta: Quick note — env var REDWOOD_BASE_URL should take precedence over SDK config file, but proxy agent may rewrite SNI/Host header. If proxy is doing TLS interception you need proxyAuth or set `NO_PROXY` for the private host. :thinking:

raj: For Node streaming we saw issues when proxy didn't support HTTP/2 or had aggressive buffering. Workaround: force HTTP/1.1 fallback — SDK has a `prefer_http2: false` flag we use in tests which resolved `ERR_HTTP2_CONNECTION` for CONNECT-style proxies.

carl: sample Node snippet that worked for us:
```js
const {RedwoodClient} = require('@redwood/sdk');
const HttpsProxyAgent = require('https-proxy-agent');
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY);
const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseURL: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL, fetchAgent: agent, prefer_http2: false });
```
Note: some SDKs call the option `agent` vs `fetchAgent` — check the language-specific README.

olga: @carl thanks — I tried similar but forgot to set `rejectUnauthorized: false` on the agent for our cert-rewriting proxy. After that streaming improved but I'm seeing latency spikes / intermittent stalls. Any tips for keep-alive or reconnect?

marta: make sure the proxy supports `CONNECT` to the final host:port; otherwise the SDK might send proxied TLS that breaks HTTP/2. Also try disabling prefix/KV caching for streaming tests (`REDWOOD_CACHE_PREFIX=false`) to isolate network vs cache behavior.

raj: Also check whether the corp proxy buffers responses until end of request. That causes small streaming chunks to be delayed. We added `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` on the upstream and it helped (if the proxy honors them).

olga: trying headers now, will report. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

devex-bot: note: opened internal ticket #INF-4721 for proxy buffering + SDK streaming; ping @netops if you need ACL or proxy config changes.

olga: fyi logging snippet I used to reproduce: 
```
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 -H 'Host: private-inference.internal' 'https://private-inference.internal/v1/stream'
```
curl shows `HTTP/1.1 502` from the proxy, but direct curl to host (no proxy) returns 200 and streams.

carl: If direct works, try `NO_PROXY=private-inference.internal` or add the FQDN. In our infra NO_PROXY sometimes needs the exact host + suffix so try both `private-inference.internal` and `.internal`.

olga: will try NO_PROXY and the additional headers, will update by EOD. thanks again!
